events.text: The Double Ninth: families climb the hills to ward off misfortune.

effects.log: At the top, the whole province spread out like a map.

choices.text: Carry an old neighbour up the hill

effects.log: She has not seen the view in ten years.

events.text: The chrysanthemum tea is ready. Tradition says it grants long life.

choices.text: Drink a cup of the tea

effects.log: Bitter and golden. You feel a year younger. Probably.

choices.text: Take a jar to an old master

effects.log: He smiles for the first time in a month.

events.text: People wear sprigs of dogwood today to keep evil away.

effects.log: Nothing evil happens. It must work.
The child wears it proudly all day.

events.text: The Double Ninth is a day to honour the old. The village elders sit in the square.

effects.log: Each of them tells you a story you will need someday.
The old soldiers light up. Tactics from forty years ago.

events.text: A rival challenges you to race up the mountain for the Double Ninth.

ok.log: You reach the top first and pour the wine.

fail.log: They win. You carry the wine.

effects.log: You arrive together, laughing.

events.text: Poets gather on the hill to write verses about exile and home.

effects.log: Your verse makes the old poets cry.
Every poem is about someone far away.

events.text: The flower market is full of chrysanthemums: white, gold, and a rare purple one.

effects.log: It blooms all autumn by your door. (−3 taels)
Some beauty should be left where it grows.

events.text: On the Double Ninth, people remember those who are gone.

choices.text: Pour a cup for an old friend

effects.log: You talk to them for an hour. It helps.
Someone should remember the forgotten.

events.text: You are carried up the hill on your elder's shoulders for the Double Ninth.

effects.log: Every tree, every bird. You are exhausting.
You miss the view. You dream of flying.

events.text: A crumbling pavilion on the hilltop where a famous poet once drank alone.

effects.log: The view has not changed in five hundred years.

choices.text: Read the poem carved in the pillar

effects.log: "Alone, I climb. Alone, I remember." You understand it better now.

events.text: A monk has had too much chrysanthemum wine and is fighting a tree.

effects.log: He thanks you and falls asleep on your shoulder.
The tree wins.

events.text: A fortune teller on the hill sells longevity charms.

effects.log: Worth it for the smiles. (−2 taels)
'Long, if you are careful.' Useful.
